name: Hyaluronic acid

lead: Hyaluronic acid is a sugar-based molecule found in skin and joints that binds large amounts of water. In serums it gives temporary surface hydration and a plumper look; in cross-linked injectable gels it is used as a dermal filler to add volume to lips, cheeks, under-eyes and folds.

Topical products hydrate the outer skin layer, which smooths the look of fine lines for a time. Fillers physically add volume, with an effect that Wikipedia says lasts around 6 to 12 months, and they have US FDA regulatory approval. A 2022 review examined topical HA for skin quality and aging, and small trials have tested oral HA supplements.

paras: Serums are applied to damp skin once or twice daily and layered under moisturizer, often alongside other actives. Fillers are administered in a clinic by trained injectors, with results visible right away and refreshed periodically as they gradually dissolve.

Topical forms are very well tolerated. Fillers commonly cause short-lived bruising, swelling and lumps at the injection site. Rare severe complications include vascular occlusion leading to tissue damage or vision loss, and outcomes are associated with injector skill.

chain: Smoother-looking skin and fewer fine lines
angle.text: Hyaluronic acid serums give temporary hydration and plumping, while injectable fillers reshape lips, cheeks and the under-eye area. It binds water, so skin looks fuller and fine lines look softer. Topical use gives short-lived hydration in studies, and fillers have extensive clinical use for volume.

lead: Hyaluronic acid (HA, hyaluronan) is an anionic, non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan found throughout connective, epithelial and neural tissue. It is unusually large, with human synovial HA averaging around 7 MDa per molecule in one description, and an average 70 kg person holds roughly 15 grams, about a third of which turns over each day [1]. It is a major component of the extracellular matrix, synovial fluid and cartilage [1].

Medically it is used for knee osteoarthritis, dry eye, wound repair and as a cosmetic filler [1]. In appearance medicine it appears in two quite different forms. Topical serums and creams are marketed for hydration and signs of skin aging, and a 2022 review examined the evidence for topical HA on skin quality and aging [2]. Cross-linked HA gels are injected as dermal fillers to add volume to lips, cheeks, folds and other areas, with an effect that Wikipedia says lasts around 6 to 12 months and that has US FDA regulatory approval [1].

Systematic reviews of HA filler trials report that most adverse events are short-lived injection-site reactions that resolve spontaneously, while rare severe complications can occur [3][4]. Oral HA supplements have also been tested in small trials for skin condition [5][6].
infobox: Topical serums; cross-linked injectable gel (dermal filler); oral supplements
About 15 g in a 70 kg adult
Cosmetic ingredient (topical); injectable fillers are regulated medical devices in the US

paras: Topical HA is a common ingredient in serums, moisturizers and masks, sold for hydration and plumping of the skin surface. A 2022 narrative review in Dermatologic Therapy summarizes the literature and clinical evidence on topical HA for skin quality and signs of aging [2].

Injectable HA fillers such as the Juvederm and Restylane lines are among the most popular cosmetic procedures in the United States, according to a 2023 systematic review [3]. HA combines with water and swells to form a gel that is used for facial wrinkles [1]. Trials include a randomized split-face study of an HA-based micro-filler for superficial wrinkles and skin quality, and a split-face comparison of polynucleotide and HA fillers for periocular rejuvenation [7][8]. A 2024 study benchmarked the injectability of commercial cross-linked HA fillers with inter-injector assessments [9].

Oral supplements containing HA, collagen and vitamin C are also marketed. A 2024 randomized placebo-controlled trial tested 5 g hydrolysed collagen with vitamin C and the same product combined with 30 mg HA over 16 weeks, measuring skin density and texture [5]. A separate randomized double-blind test examined oral HA and skin conditions [6]. A 2025 meta-analysis addressed collagen-based supplements and skin hydration and elasticity [10].

HA injections are used for knee osteoarthritis (viscosupplementation). A 2023 network meta-analysis compared corticosteroids, HA and platelet-rich plasma for knee osteoarthritis, and other trials compared HA with PRP in hip osteoarthritis and in knee osteoarthritis [11][12][13]. A systematic review addressed HA, corticosteroids and PRP in temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis [14]. HA viscoelastic products are also used in cataract surgery, and registered trials cover products such as Healon5 and DisCoVisc and Monovisc injections for shoulder, ankle and hip osteoarthritis [15][16][17][18].

Wikipedia states that reviews as of 2023 found either insufficient or limited positive clinical evidence for HA in healing chronic wounds, including burns, diabetic foot ulcers and surgical skin repairs [1]. A 2023 trial tested HA gel with photobiomodulation after gingivectomy [19].

For fillers, randomized trials generally compare products with each other or with controls, and are the main basis for regulatory approval. A 2016 systematic review of randomized trials covered the physicochemical properties and applications of HA across medical fields [20]. The effect of fillers is temporary because the gel is gradually broken down, which Wikipedia puts at about 6 to 12 months [1].

For topical products, the 2022 review describes the clinical evidence for skin quality benefits and notes how it ranges from hydration to appearance of lines [2]. The widely repeated figure that HA holds about a thousand times its weight in water is a laboratory-derived claim; none of the clinical studies reviewed here tests that figure directly.

A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis in Cureus examined adverse events after HA dermal filler injection to the face using 19 randomized trials, stating that most outcomes are mild and resolve but that rare severe complications can be irreversible [3]. A 2024 systematic review in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery analyzed 48 higher-level studies, classified events as expected reactions, product- or technique-related events and severe adverse events, and found most events were short-lived injection-site reactions that resolved on their own within weeks, with filler type and technique affecting their occurrence [4].
Topical HA is described as well tolerated; a retail deodorant containing HA on DailyMed carries general external-use and irritation warnings [21].

HA is a humectant polymer that binds water. In cartilage, aggrecan binds to HA and the resulting negatively charged aggregates imbibe water, giving cartilage its resistance to compression; in synovial fluid, HA contributes viscosity and lubrication [1]. In wounds it supports cell migration, inflammation response and angiogenesis, and is abundant in granulation tissue [1]. Low-molecular-weight fragments produced during inflammation can activate immune cells, as examined in a 2021 review on HA in inflammation [22].
Filler properties depend on cross-linking and rheology, covered in a 2023 review in Clinics in Plastic Surgery [23].

HA differs from other glycosaminoglycans in being non-sulfated, forming at the plasma membrane rather than in the Golgi apparatus, and reaching very large sizes. It can be chemically modified at its carboxyl, primary alcohol and N-acetyl groups to improve biocompatibility, permeation and sustained drug release [1].

Forum material in the sources reviewed treats HA mainly as a joint supplement or injection rather than a skin product. T Nation posters describe taking supplements with hyaluronic acid among joint ingredients, planning HA injections for knee or shoulder problems, or taking HA for connective tissue [24][25][26][27]. HA fillers are part of the broader cosmetic procedure market discussed in appearance communities, but no community threads on fillers were available in the sources reviewed.

Cosmetic: a 2023 meta-analysis of 19 randomized trials on adverse events after facial HA filler injection [3]; a 2024 systematic review of 48 randomized studies on filler adverse events [4]; a randomized prospective multicenter study of an HA micro-filler for superficial wrinkles [7]; a split-face trial of polynucleotide versus HA filler in the periocular area with 27 participants [8]; and a 2024 randomized trial of oral collagen with or without HA on skin parameters [5].

Medical: numerous randomized trials and reviews of intra-articular HA in knee, hip and temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis [11][12][13][14], and registered trials of viscosupplements and ophthalmic viscosurgical devices [15][16][17][18].
